lead.t: Cranial nerve VI palsy (horizontal diplopia): The abducens nerve has a long intracranial course; it is stretched by raised pressure.

snip.t: Cranial nerve VI palsy (horizontal diplopia): The abducens nerve has a long intracranial course; it is stretched by raised pressure.
Abducens nerve palsy may be a nonlocalizing sign of elevated ICP.
The mass effect can produce an obstructive hydrocephalus, as well as impinge upon adjacent structures, such as the abducens nerve (CN VI) in this case.
